Subject: DPA redline — runtime payload logging / subprocessor scope

Hi Lukas,

Thanks for the call last week. Our legal team reviewed Redwood's standard DPA and attached a marked-up redline (Solstice_DPA_redline_v2.pdf). There are two items we cannot accept without explicit confirmation from your product/security teams:

1) Runtime payload logging: the proposed clause in Section 4.2 allows Redwood to store inference payloads and telemetry for troubleshooting. We need a stricter limit — Solstice requires that raw inference prompts or documents originating from customers not be retained longer than 30 days, and where retention is necessary it must be encrypted and accessible only via our KMS keys or masked/hashes.

2) Subprocessor disclosure: please confirm the full list of subprocessors that may have access to runtime telemetry (including any analytics or logging vendors). We need an allowlist and notification for new subprocessors.

Could you route this to your product and security folks and let us know whether Redwood can accept the changes or propose alternative language? We're trying to keep the engagement on schedule for the end-of-month signature.

Attached: Solstice_DPA_redline_v2.pdf (annotated).

Best,
Maria Ortega
Head of Legal Operations
Solstice Systems

Lukas — my read and proposed approach below. Longish but want to be explicit so legal has workable language.

Quick summary:
- Security requirement is reasonable: we can't broadly promise no retention without clarification of "retention for troubleshooting". We can agree to not retain raw customer content beyond a short window and to provide stronger controls.
- Must scope what we call "runtime telemetry" vs "customer content". If inference inputs contain customer PII, they are customer content. Telemetry should be limited to metadata (timings, error codes, token counts) and fingerprints/hashes of inputs, not full prompts.

Minimum commitments we can sign to (recommendation):
1) Raw customer inputs (complete prompts or uploaded artifacts) will not be stored in cleartext beyond 14 days by default. We can retain cryptographic hashes or deterministic fingerprints for up to 90 days for debugging and regression tracing.
2) For customers requiring shorter windows, we will offer a per-account configuration to set raw-input retention to 0/7/30 days.
3) Any retention of raw inputs will be encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys (KMS) when requested via enterprise contract addendum. By default, Redwood-managed KMS is used unless customer elects otherwise.
4) Subprocessor disclosure: we will provide a current allowlist of subprocessors (logging, analytics, monitoring, cloud infra) as a schedule to the DPA and commit to a 30-day notification window before onboarding a new subprocessor affecting runtime telemetry.
5) Auditability: we will produce audit logs showing access to stored telemetry and provide SOC 2 attestation references in the legal appendix.

Suggested clause language (short form) to offer Solstice: 
"Redwood will not persist raw customer inputs (including prompts, documents or files submitted to inference endpoints) in readable form beyond 14 days by default. Redwood may retain cryptographic hashes or fingerprints of inputs for up to 90 days for debugging and regression purposes. Customers may elect a shorter retention window (including immediate deletion) via per-account configuration or as specified in an addendum that enables customer-managed encryption keys. Redwood will provide a current list of subprocessors with a 30-day notice period for changes and will produce audit logs of access to stored telemetry upon valid customer request."

Open questions for product: does the 14-day default break any existing features? How hard is it to expose the per-account flag?

I've attached a short file with inline suggested redline text: security_commentary_redline.txt.

—Olga
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Lukas / Olga — product perspective below. TL;DR: we can accept Olga's recommended commitments with a small implementation scope and feature gating.

Current behavior (very high level):
- We persist a short prefix of prompts for tracing (default retention 60 days) and aggregated telemetry (error rates, latencies) indefinitely.
- We also store KV-cache snapshots and occasionally short request bodies for debugging in a limited S3 bucket (accessed by ops/admins).

Impact / implementation plan: 
- Move default raw-input retention from 60 -> 14 days: easy to implement — change retention policy on the S3 lifecycle and add a pipeline job to scrub older items. ETA: 2 weeks engineering (can be delivered as a patch release).
- Expose per-account retention flag (0/7/14/30): medium effort — needs UI + API + infra gating. ETA: 4–6 weeks if prioritized.
- Customer-managed KMS support for runtime storage: heavier (KMS key passthrough + access controls). ETA: 8–12 weeks depending on legal requirements.
- Subprocessor allowlist: we can produce a current list immediately; 30-day notification is operationally fine.

Recommendation: Accept Olga's proposed language but offer 14-day default (not 30) with option for Solstice to request shorter retention or customer-managed KMS in the addendum. This hits a lower risk posture while being responsive.

Proposed outreach to Solstice: send the suggested clause from Olga but change default to 14 days and include a timeline footnote (we can change default retention within 2 weeks and provide per-account flag within 6 weeks).

If legal signs off, I'll prepare a short product note and runbook for the ops team and schedule the engineering tickets.

—Kimberly Park
Head of Product, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Maria / Solstice legal — thanks for the redline and for your patience while we assessed internally.

We can accept the high-level goal in your note with the following proposed commitment (we've included our legal/security language below and attached a marked-up doc redline_v3.docx):

1) Redwood will not persist raw customer inputs (including prompts, documents, or files submitted to inference endpoints) in readable form beyond 14 days by default.
2) Redwood may retain cryptographic hashes or fingerprints of inputs for up to 90 days for debugging and regression purposes.
3) For customers requiring a shorter retention window or customer-managed encryption keys, Redwood will provide a contractual addendum to enable per-account retention settings and KMS integration.
4) Redwood will provide a current allowlist of subprocessors as a schedule to the DPA and give 30 days' notice prior to onboarding any subprocessor that would access runtime telemetry.
5) Redwood will produce audit logs of access to stored telemetry and can provide SOC 2 attestation references on request.

Product & security have signed off on the above and we can implement the default retention change within ~2 weeks from signature; per-account flags and KMS options will require additional implementation time (we included rough ETA in the attached).

Please see attached redline_v3.docx for the exact language. If that looks acceptable, we can loop in legal to finalize and target execution before month-end.
